notes.text: Poach in batches of 4 and hold them in warm water.

move.title: Eight eggs, poached and held
move.body: Çılbır is a Turkish breakfast: soft poached eggs on cool garlic yogurt, with butter warmed with Aleppo pepper poured over the top and bread to drag through it. The skill is poaching for a crowd: you'll poach eight eggs in two batches and hold them in warm water so they all reach the table together. Pasteurized eggs make the soft yolks safe.

why.title: Drain the loose white
why.body: The thin, watery part of the white makes ragged wisps. Tipped into a slotted spoon for a few seconds, it drains away, leaving the firm white that holds its shape.

why.title: Water at 180–190°F
why.body: Small bubbles on the bottom, none breaking hard. Hotter water tears the white; cooler water lets it spread.

why.title: Hold in warm water
why.body: Poached eggs keep 20 minutes in 150°F water without cooking further, so a whole batch can be served at once.

why.title: Pasteurized for soft yolks
why.body: Pasteurized eggs are heated in the shell just enough to kill bacteria, so a soft yolk is safe for everyone at the table.

wrong.fix: The loose white wasn't drained, or the eggs were old. Strain each egg first.
They poached too long or the holding water was too hot. Hold at about 150°F.
The heat was too high. Warm it gently; Aleppo pepper scorches fast.

quiz.q: Why drain each egg in a slotted spoon first?
choices: The watery white drains off, so no wisps
quiz.explain: The firm white holds its shape.

quiz.q: How do you serve 8 poached eggs at once?
choices: Hold the first batch in 150°F water
Keep them on a cold plate
Soft yolks are safe for everyone

steps.text: Grate or mince the garlic to a paste and stir it into the yogurt with the salt. Spread it on 4 plates and let it come to cool room temperature.
steps.look: A thick swoosh of yogurt on each plate.

steps.text: Bring the poaching water and vinegar to 180–190°F in the large pot. Fill the bowl with 150°F tap-hot water for holding.
Crack an egg into the small bowl, then tip it into the slotted spoon over the sink for 5 seconds.
Lower the egg into the water from the spoon. Repeat with 3 more, a few seconds apart, washing your hands after cracking.
Lift each egg in turn and press the white.

target.look: Whites fully set, with no clear parts; yolks soft

steps.text: Move them to the holding water. Poach the second batch the same way.
Melt the butter over low heat, take it off the heat, and stir in the Aleppo pepper.
Blot each egg on a paper towel and set 2 on each plate of yogurt. Spoon over the pepper butter and scatter the dill.
steps.look: Glossy red butter running over white eggs and yogurt.
